title: Conformity Traps and the Formation of Independent Judgment
abstract: arXiv:2608.18981v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: I study why some groups---polities and organizations alike---sustain independent judgment while others fall into conformity traps. Social approval can suppress not only the expression of independent judgment but also the upstream practice that keeps such judgment available: maintaining judgment generates visible questioning, and observers cannot distinguish diligence from opposition. Because suspicion falls when questioning is common, the same desire for approval can sustain a questioning culture or a conformity trap. The model separates maintaining judgment from acting on it when novelty arrives. When the decision to act is uniquely determined, I give primitive conditions for coexistence; in a logit--proportional benchmark, a single inequality is necessary and sufficient. translated_title: 从众陷阱与独立判断的形成
translated_abstract: 摘要：我研究为什么有些群体——无论是政治体还是组织——能够维持独立判断，而其他群体则陷入从众陷阱。社会认可不仅会抑制独立判断的表达，还会抑制维持这种判断可用的上游实践：维持判断会产生可见的质疑，而观察者无法区分勤奋与反对。当质疑变得普遍时，怀疑会减少，因此同样的认可渴望既能维持一种质疑文化，也能导致从众陷阱。该模型将维持判断与在新事物出现时采取行动区分开来。当行动决策是唯一确定时，我给出了共存的原初条件；在对数比——比例基准模型中，一个单一不等式是必要且充分的。主要贡献是动态性的。在交错修订下，判断存量会被继承：保护异议会立即释放现有判断——但带有负面效应。
tldr: 本文通过一个动态模型揭示了社会认可如何既可能导致从众陷阱，也可能维持质疑文化，并指出交错修订下保护异议会立即释放现有判断但伴随负面后果。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through a dynamic model how social approval can either lead to conformity traps or sustain a questioning culture, and shows that under staggered revision, protecting dissent releases existing judgment immediately but with negative consequences.
